history.summary: A modern temple complex created by the Indian Oil Corporation - built by current and former workers and officers of the Gujarat Refinery, per visitor accounts - and now maintained by Reliance Petrochemical Industries, located inside the Petrochemical Township near the IPCL sports complex. The name 'Tapovan' suggests a place of penance and meditation. The complex holds shrines to many deities (Shiva, Durga, Mansa Devi, Lakshmi-Narayana, Tirupati Balaji, Navgraha, Satyanarayan, Murugan, Ayyappa) in colourful South-Indian-influenced architecture, plus a meditation hall, a gaushala and landscaped gardens. One visitor account says construction took about 7-8 years (verify). Entry for non-township visitors may require township assistance or permission (verify).

town_description: Vadodara (formerly Baroda) is a major city in Gujarat on the Vishwamitri river, famed as the cultural capital of the state. It was the seat of the Gaekwad rulers, whose patronage left palaces, museums and temples across the city. The city's northern outskirts host the Gujarat Refinery petrochemical township, home to this temple.

travel.railway: Vadodara Junction (~7 km, per visitor accounts)
travel.road: On Gujarat Refinery Road, behind the IPCL Sports Complex, Petrochemical Township; reachable by auto-rickshaw/taxi from Vadodara city
